product_tiers.notes: Basic OAuth apps can be created without review; sensitive scopes may trigger review.

summary: GitHub provides a self‑serve OAuth app registration flow that requires a logged‑in GitHub account and no paid plan; most apps are approved instantly unless they request sensitive scopes.

time.setup_notes: Registration is done via the GitHub UI; exact time varies by developer.

approval_wait.label: None for basic install · Marketplace: not published
approval_wait.notes: GitHub does not publish a wait time for basic OAuth app approval; organizations can enable approval policies but no timeline is documented.

prerequisites.notes: A free GitHub account is sufficient to register an OAuth app.

steps.title: Sign in to GitHub
steps.detail: Log in to your GitHub account at https://github.com.

steps.title: Navigate to Developer Settings
steps.detail: Go to Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps.

steps.title: Create a new OAuth App
steps.detail: Click "New OAuth App" and fill in the app name, homepage URL, and callback URL (must use HTTPS except for localhost).

steps.title: Save the client ID and client secret
steps.detail: After creation, copy the generated client ID and client secret for use in your application.

steps.title: Configure scopes
steps.detail: Select the required scopes for your app; avoid unnecessary sensitive scopes to prevent review.

steps.title: Test the OAuth flow
steps.detail: Direct users to https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize with your client_id and requested scopes, then exchange the code at https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token.

scopes.notes: Sensitive scope; may require organization approval.
